drivingQuestion: What does Rav Yeimar's ruling teach that the mishna about consecration does not?
outcomeNote: This unit answers the מאי קא משמע לן of the preceding unit and has no question of its own.

segments.he: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא, הָתָם הוּא דְּסָבַר מִצְוָה קָא עָבֵידְנָא, אֲבָל לְעִנְיַן זַבּוֹנֵי — מִצְוָה דְּגוּפֵיהּ לָא (זבין) [מְזַבֵּין] אִינִישׁ, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.
segments.en: The Gemara explains: It is necessary, «lest you say» that it is only «there,» when one consecrates his property, that the halakha «is» that his phylacteries are taken, «as he thinks» to himself: «I am performing a mitzva,» and therefore he intended for his phylacteries to be included. «But with regard to a sale, a person» would «not sell» an item used for «a mitzva that» he performs with «his body» without explicitly stating so. The Gemara therefore «teaches us» by means of the above incident that phylacteries are included in the property of such a sale.

moves.summary: floats the view that consecration and sale differ, since only the consecrator thinks he is performing a mitzva
moves.about: Rav Yeimar's ruling teaches that phylacteries are included even in a sale, and not only where the owner consecrates and thinks he is performing a mitzva

moves.summary: Rav Yeimar's ruling teaches that phylacteries are included in a sale as well
moves.about: why Rav Yeimar's ruling is not superfluous, answering the difficulty raised in the preceding unit
